transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jamal (Redwood CSM); Daniel (CTO), Mia (Head of Platform), Samir (SRE), Erica (Legal)

Summary: informal renewal/expansion check-in — customer is approaching contract renewal in Q1, looking at a 2x capacity top-up, adding EU region, wants private VPC option for PCI-ish workflows, plus a failover/fallback plan. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted, and a proposed benchmark run. Agreed next steps and action items.

00:00:05 Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:00:08 Daniel: yeah loud and clear, thanks Alex.
00:00:12 Alex: cool, quick agenda — status of current usage, renewal timing, proposed capacity bump and geo add, open security questions, then wrap with next steps. if anything else flag it.
00:00:25 Mia: sounds good. we're on a 60 day notice window, renewal Jan 15 window but we can be flexible. main ask is we need predictable perf for peak checkout flows in EU and fallback if us-east flakes.
00:00:40 Priya: mmhmm, got it. can you remind us of current qps and token mix? last snapshot we had from your prod logs was ~420 qps avg and peaks at 1.8k during promo spikes?
00:00:52 Samir: that's right, those numbers line up. token length is...varies, but typical is 160 tokens per request in the chat flows. Some reranking jobs hit 800 tokens.
00:01:05 Alex: thanks. ok so rough ask i heard — 2x baseline capacity, EU region activation, and a VPC/private path for sensitive payloads. also you mentioned wanting stronger SLA for p50/p95 latency during promos.
00:01:18 Daniel: yes, plus a contractual guarantee around failover routing — if primary region is overloaded, we want automatic fallback to a compatible model in another region with bounded failover time.
00:01:29 Priya: that maps well to Redwood features — we have routing policies, canary rollouts, and option for model variants for graceful degradation. small note: the automatic fallback latency depends on how similar the model variant is and whether KV cache warmup is needed.
00:01:45 Mia: explain the KV cache warmup bit — is that a big hit on failover?
00:01:49 Priya: so, KV cache (our internal term for the key-value attention cache) is per-host, per-request sequence. when you route live traffic to a different region or node that hasn't seen that conversational prefix, the first few tokens there may be slightly slower. we mitigate with prefix caching and warmup, but there is a short runway. typical p95 delta can be 60-150ms depending on model/seq length.
00:02:12 Samir: hmm, that could push us over our 600ms target for checkout. any tactics?
00:02:16 Priya: couple of levers — smaller model variants in the fallback (lower latency, cost), aggressive prefix KV caching between regions for common prompts, or prewarmed reserved instances for the promoted window. there's also a 'burst buffer' option in Dedicated configuration.
00:02:33 Alex: to add, Redwood Dedicated lets you reserve GPU pools with guaranteed concurrency, which avoids noisy neighbor issues. Dedicated + autoscale burst gives predictable tail latencies at higher cost.
00:02:44 Daniel: cost is a big concern. last year we tried BigCloudAI but the egress pricing and unpredictability killed the unit economics. what's Redwood's neat middle ground?
00:02:55 Alex: we try to provide cost-aware knobs — batching, prefix caching, and quantization recommendations via Redwood Optimize can drive down per-token charges. we can show modeled impact on your traffic in the pricing worksheet.
00:03:07 Mia: are those quantization suggestions safe for our reranking jobs? we've had hallucination/regression worries in the past when devs tried 8-bit.
00:03:14 Priya: totally legitimate. Optimize suggests model/quantization tie-ins by workload; for reranking/QA we recommend mixed strategy — keep 16-bit for rerank-heavy paths, push 8-bit for short chat responses. we check for quality regressions with prompt-level evals.
00:03:30 Samir: ok. security checklist — SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS, and residency. Erica's here for contract language.
00:03:38 Erica: hi — the main legal ask is auditability and proof of data segregation. for the EU region we need to ensure logs don't contain cross-customer PII and a clause about data residency. also curious about HSM support for keys.
00:03:52 Jamal: for audit logs we can stream token-level usage to your SIEM; Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for key wrapping. we also offer retention controls on logs. i'll follow up with a docs bundle.
00:04:07 Erica: great, please include sample SLA/annex language for retention.
00:04:11 Alex: noted. ok back to capacity — if you're targeting a 2x top-up, we want to size for your peak promo window plus a safety buffer. Priya, do you want to walk sizing assumptions?
00:04:22 Priya: sure. baseline numbers -> current peak 1.8k qps at 160 tokens average — with 2x you'd want reserved concurrency to hit ~3.6k peak. on modern A100-style nodes we estimate x tokens/sec per GPU; if you use quantized variants we could lower GPU per qps. recommend a mixed capacity: 60% hosted burst for normal, 40% reserved Dedicated for promos. that keeps cost down and provides guaranteed headroom.
00:04:50 Mia: curious how quickly Dedicated can scale for a promo — is it autoscale or manual provisioning?
00:04:55 Priya: Dedicated supports autoscale policies; provisioning new nodes in cloud regions can take minutes depending on availability. if you want true instant headroom we do a burst buffer (pre-warmed nodes) that sits idle but ready. it's expensive but fastest.
00:05:08 Samir: can we do a hybrid where browsers on EU talk to EU region and non-sensitive payloads to hosted, sensitive to Private/VPC?
00:05:14 Priya: yes. We can route by tenant or route attribute; you can set policy rules to send requests with a sensitivity flag to Private VPC endpoints. routing happens in the control plane, with fallbacks to designated variants.
00:05:25 Daniel: cool. what about network topology — do you support VPC peering or private links? we need private connectivity from our infra to Redwood Private.
00:05:33 Jamal: we support VPC peering and private endpoint options across major clouds; on-prem deployments use an appliance or secure tunnel. also we can do IP allowlists and mutual TLS.
00:05:42 Erica: any penalties for early termination if we sign a longer committed capacity?
00:05:46 Alex: contract terms are negotiable. typical reserved commitments have a minimum term and breakage is handled via prorated fees; we'll share a sample amendment.
00:05:54 Daniel: ok. let's talk timeline — we want EU up and running before Black Friday cycle in late November next year, but first priority is Jan renewal. are there minimum lead times?
00:06:05 Priya: for a new region activation plus Private VPC we recommend 6-10 weeks end-to-end for provisioning, security review, and partner approvals; if you want a quicker pilot, we can spin up a hosted EU zone in 2-3 weeks for smoke tests, then migrate to Private.
00:06:20 Mia: that works. pilot in hosted EU to validate latency and then switch to Private for production.
00:06:25 Samir: benchmark — we want actual p50/p95 with our payloads and a simulated promo load. can Redwood run that?
00:06:31 Priya: yes, we can coordinate a benchmark window. ideally you provide a masked test set and traffic pattern; we run three runs (baseline hosted, dedicated config, fallback scenario) and share the logs and a breakdown by token cost and latency.
00:06:46 Alex: we'll include a spreadsheet modelling the cost per 1M tokens across the configs.
00:06:50 Daniel: good. competitor note — BigCloudAI offered cheaper on-paper rates but their fallback plan was manual and egress was onerous. any gotchas with Redwood's cross-region egress?
00:07:00 Jamal: cross-region egress is explicit in pricing; we can structure traffic flows to minimize cross-region KV cache misses and keep most traffic local. also we can recommend data partitioning to reduce egress.
00:07:12 Mia: what about SLOs? you mentioned p95 targets earlier, are those contractual?
00:07:17 Alex: we offer SLA-backed uptime and can commit to latency targets on Dedicated via a service level annex; the latency SLA is negotiated per workload because token lengths and models change the baseline.
00:07:30 Erica: legal will want measurable SLAs with credits spelled out.
00:07:34 Alex: yes — we'll include a template SLA with credit mechanics to start.
00:07:39 Daniel: okay, let's capture the decision we need to make: 1) renewal quantity (2x commit?) 2) EU hosted pilot or Private from day one? 3) pricing and contract language. Anything else?
00:07:50 Mia: fallback policy: we want automatic fallback to a compatible model in <30s with max p95 penalty of 200ms. is that realistic?
00:07:58 Priya: the <30s — if you mean time to failover, that is doable; p95 penalty 200ms is optimistic but possibly achievable with aggressive prefix caching and prewarmed nodes. need validation in a benchmark.
00:08:12 Samir: can we do a canary failover test as part of the pilot?
00:08:15 Priya: absolutely — we can simulate region outage and measure impact.
00:08:18 Alex: ok those are good asks. let's talk numbers — i won't quote final here but ballpark the 2x reserved with mixed burst model increases committed monthly run-rate by ~1.7x to 2.2x depending on quantization and batching. we'll quantify in the worksheet.
00:08:33 Daniel: understood. on billing model — we prefer committed capacity rather than strict per-token because it gives predictability. can we do a top-up model mid-term?
00:08:42 Alex: yes, we support mid-term amendments to increase capacity. pricing tiers get better with longer terms / larger commits.
00:08:49 Erica: for the EU region we need contractual language about data residency and audit rights. also want to pin retention windows.
00:08:57 Jamal: we'll include the legal annex.
00:08:59 Mia: one more ops question — how are model rollouts managed? we need ability to freeze updates in production and control model version pins.
00:09:06 Priya: Redwood Console supports pinning model versions per route, canary fraction rollouts, and automatic rollback on regression triggers. we also have tracing hooks for token-level attribution.
00:09:18 Samir: tracing hooks — can they be forwarded to our tracer or SIEM?
00:09:21 Priya: yes we have a webhook and direct integrations for major tracing systems.
00:09:25 Daniel: ok. any red flags?
00:09:28 Mia: nothing blocking but we need benchmark evidence for the failover latency claim.
00:09:32 Alex: agreed. action plan recap in a minute.
00:09:36 Daniel: quick question about encryption at rest — we want HSM-backed keys in EU. is that supported?
00:09:40 Jamal: yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported for Private; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping in many cases. specifics in the security docs.
00:09:51 Erica: please include a diagram of key flow and where logs live.
00:09:55 Jamal: will do.
00:09:57 Alex: ok let's pivot to the benchmark scope so Priya can capture requirements.
00:10:00 Priya: for benchmark we need: masked dataset with typical prompt lengths, target QPS profile (steady + promo spike), list of sensitive routes to exercise Private path, and desired metrics (p50/p95/p99, token cost). we'll run three configs: hosted eu pilot, dedicated with prewarm, and fallback test with KV-cache cold start.
00:10:20 Mia: i'll assemble the masked dataset and the QPS profiles. Samir will help with traffic shaping.
00:10:25 Samir: yep.
00:10:28 Priya: timeline: we can run the benchmark in the week of Dec 8 if that's ok. we need test data by Dec 5.
00:10:35 Mia: Dec 5 works for us.
00:10:37 Alex: awesome. any procurement gating items? Erica?
00:10:39 Erica: we'll need to review the draft amendment and the annex for residency. prefer 7 business days for legal review cycles.
00:10:47 Alex: noted. we'll aim to send docs Dec 3 so you have time.
00:10:51 Daniel: ok, wrap up then.
00:10:53 Alex: recap: Redwood to send pricing worksheet and draft amendment by Dec 3; Priya to schedule and run benchmark w/c Dec 8 using customer test set; customer to confirm EU region list and provide masked dataset by Dec 5; Jamal to share security + SOC2/ISO docs including KMS/HSM notes. next sync to review benchmark results and finalize amendment.
00:11:15 Mia: that covers it. thanks.
00:11:17 Samir: thanks all.
00:11:19 Erica: thanks.

[--- End of recorded segment (pace: meeting wraps early with some post-call side chat) ---]
